attractors.instead: carry the idea on type, a real object or a colour field. If you keep a disc, give it a light source and a surface. Name the product after what it does or a concrete thing it owns (a place, a tool, a material), not light poetry. Pick the subject from the request, never from an example.

beat-cause.instead: name an act as the cause ("the cursor hits Send on the card in beat 1"), not "then" or "it cuts to".

beat-earns-time.instead: write per beat the role, the persuasion move (pain agitation, negative contrast, future pacing, social proof, risk reversal, inevitability) and the feeling arc (anxiety to relief, curiosity to payoff). A beat with neither is cut.

claim-backed.instead: cut the number, or demonstrate it in the same beat: "26 looks" needs 26 looks on screen.

cta-last-short.instead: keep the world moving under the end card (see moving-tail).

hook-payoff.instead: tease the number in the hook, show it last. Front-load the strong word. Order the middle by rising surprise.

legible-effect.instead: enlarge it, lengthen it or cut it: a displacement wash on smooth material, a glow on dark content or a blinds slat in 0.4 s reads as nothing.

motion-register.instead: write the register in the brief. A hype film with every beat moving the same way is still monotone.

name-three-reject-first.instead: write the three in the brief: a capture, the real data, a counter that ticks, a hand-keyed reveal. The first answer is rise plus fade; the third is usually the film.

no-emdash-on-screen.instead: a comma, a period or a middle dot.

no-inventory.instead: tagline to hook, pain to the problem beat, how it works to build, best stat to the payoff, transformation to the payoff, CTA to the end.

owner-decides.instead: write the decision as a line under '## Declared' in the film's DESIGN.md (font, type-scale, ui-scale, camera); the acceptance rows and the judge then follow it and print which line they followed.

scene-budget.instead: set the count from the brand tempo: a calm brand is slow with few scenes, playful is fast with many. Accelerate toward the climax, then hold it longer than anything else.

shot-length-varies.instead: tighten cutting through the build, release on the payoff. Pacing is readable, not rushed: a quick cut is a hard cut between held beats, never a shorter read. A captured clip or a UI screen dwells at least 1.2 s, and held text keeps its read time (rule readable-hold).

show-real-thing.instead: render a mini-scene so the viewer watches the thing work (a value changes and the output updates; the real word cycles through colours). If a cursor clicks, the next frames show what the click did. For a real product, capture the real UI. For an invented product the brief asks you to invent the UI: design it as a real interface (the builder skill of the ladder, real-looking data, controls that do something; the frame rejects web-page patterns, the UI parts do not), then place it in the frame. Only fake chrome with no function, or a placeholder label, is the pitfall. Build a screen as a real interface first, then place it under the density budget: a fragment for the shot with large type, few elements, real imagery. Set each cell to the source's own aspect ratio so object-fit: cover neither crops nor letterboxes. A dark capture goes on a dark surface.

style-not-content.instead: write what the reference does (a cut every 0.8 s, a warm key light, a push on the last word) and rebuild it with your own subject, words and marks.

thread.instead: name the thread before the first still. Object: the caret writes, then expands into the panel. Type line: the headline's last word is the next shot's first. Colour: one accent passes from a word to a ground to a button. Rhythm: every cut lands on one pulse. Unfinished sentence: no clause finishes at a cut.
thread.range: 1 to 2 threads, named in the brief: an object, a type line, a colour or a rhythm

three-materials.instead: take a different material for each of A, B and C, not three colours of one idea.

accent-share.instead: put the accent on one thing: a caret, an eyebrow, one numeral, the CTA. On an accent-coloured ground, do not use the accent for emphasis (blue on blue vanishes).

archetype-rotation.instead: change three or more of layout, scale, value, ground, hue and motion between neighbours; value is the strongest variety lever.

asymmetry.instead: a split (headline left, artifact right), a corner anchor, big left and small right. A 6/6 split is the equal grid again. Left-align anything multi-line or list-like.

first-frame.instead: put the thread, the first word or the brand colour in frame 0, and start the sound at 0 as well.

graphic-is-subject.instead: bring the picture forward and make the type a caption. A picture behind the content is scenery. Quantity: a bar whose length is the figure (a count-up beside it, never instead). Proportion: a ring, an arc, a filled grid. Change: a line or a before and after side by side. Flow: nodes and connectors that draw on. Real thing: a capture, a photo, a clipped screenshot.

ground-hue.instead: give two or more worlds a ground in another hue family, taken from the palette, and let the accent carry the thread. The reference's own changes are in the line the draft prints (bin/vawe refs frames <id> shows its palette per shot).

hero-plus-proof.instead: put the product and photos at hero size in the acts where the reference shows them; real photos, never an invented image. The background is not empty: a radial glow, a real ground field from prompts/moves, oversized ghost type bleeding off the frame, or a subtle panel, 2 to 5 decoratives. A decorative that moves does so with the beat's own element motion, not a drift of its own. Decoratives never carry information. Never a big word centred on empty space.

hierarchy.instead: lower the contrast or the weight of supporting text instead of only shrinking it. If you read the support first, it is too loud. Use bigger type, not a wider box: the glyphs filled only 67 percent of the declared boxes.

icon-family.instead: a text-only list of named things is a missed layer. A mono logo the same value as the ground is invisible, so keep a light and a dark variant.

image-source-order.instead: a clean gradient beats a mismatched photo; if a beat reads fine on a plain field, add no image. Generated images get the same treatment and grade as any other.

image-treatment.instead: use the lightest treatment that does the job; an over-graded image is as off as a raw one.

licensed-assets.instead: capture the real product UI. Read a new source's own licence; sites are listed in resources/README.md. Record the source and licence of every bed in assets/music/credits.json before it goes under a film.

living-ground.instead: put two or three large soft blobs, clearly lighter or more saturated than the ground, behind the content: the Grounds moves in prompts/moves/README.md (gradient-mesh-field, aurora-drift, light-pool, grain-field). Keep the text on a calm part of the blob. Shader and noise sources and their licences: resources/README.md. The ground is a field behind the content: it does not need to move, and a ground drift is never what keeps a hold alive (rule live-hold). Light that should read as a lens effect (bloom, flare, a pool of light on a screen) is real lens work (prompts/moves/lens.md), not a CSS gradient.

logo-prominence.instead: size by optical balance (a circle looks smaller than a square of the same box). Keep a light variant for dark grounds and a dark variant for light grounds. The end card keeps moving with the world.

one-focal-point.instead: let the second thing arrive after the first lands. Brighter means contrast against the ground, not luminance: white type on a white field is not the focal point.

palette-from-brand.instead: read the site's CSS tokens before an eyedrop: CSS beats pixels for anything declared. Tint the neutrals (a warm ink, a cool grey); never pure `#000`, `#fff` or `#808080` the brief did not ask for.
palette-from-brand.range: a family (warm neutral, cool neutral, saturated, mono plus accent, duotone) with a ground, a surface, three text levels and one accent

readable-hold.instead: hold each line max(1.2 s, words / 3), prose words x 0.6 s, from its last settled character, and cut past 8 words; keep the move quick (taste/craft/typography.md). The clock starts when the last character settles. Motion stays quick; exits still run shorter than entrances.

readable-text-size.instead: raise the font until the cap height is 6 percent of the frame (about 93 px at 1080p), never shrink the line (taste/craft/typography.md). A mock screen whose UI is the subject goes in a `data-ui` element and keeps its real proportions: 3 percent, or the `ui-scale` the film's DESIGN.md declares.

real-optics.instead: use the lens surface (prompts/moves/lens.md) for bloom, fringe, focus and flares; a CSS blur or radial gradient is not a lens.

safe-margin.instead: move the element in; check the real box after layout, not the source.

shared-edges.instead: snap the blocks to one margin and one indent; centre a lone title instead of nudging it.

surface-spec.instead: build a reusable surface standalone first (`bin/vawe frame <page> --at t` renders one frame in seconds); glass needs a moving gradient behind it. Check: every colour is in the palette, families and weights match with no silent swap, radii match the scale, no forbidden component appears.

text-breathing.instead: leave one or two beats with no words: let the product, the object or the ground carry them. Cut text from the beat that says the same thing twice.

text-contrast.instead: keep drifting background elements off any text during its hold, or park the text over a flat part of the field.

theme-source.instead: ask for a reference or a theme when none is given; take the palette seed from the brief's Design system section. Never fall back to plain grey.

type-scale.instead: pick three sizes (hero, support, label) and set every text to one of them.

type-setting.instead: set display type to letter-spacing: -0.03em. For a dark scene, drop body weight from 400 to 350 and open leading by 0.05 to 0.1 by hand.

typeface-default.instead: run `node scripts/brand/kit.mjs <url> <name> --init` and use the kit's face; with no brand, look at the bundled faces in assets/fonts, name the signal you want and reject your first instinct.

typeface-system.instead: give each face a role like a colour has; use tabular numerals on counters so the width does not jitter; emphasise inside a line by recolouring at the same weight, not a heavier bold.

value-dominance.instead: on a light canvas use bolder borders (2 px or more), stronger structure and full-saturation accent hits; do not swap the values of a dark design.

visual-style-one.instead: justify the style from the brand's own site; a register you cannot justify there is the wrong one: restudy, do not guess.

weight-contrast.instead: use the full 100 to 900 range the loaded faces carry; thin weights shimmer in motion and compression.

whitespace.instead: name what the empty area does in one clause. If a bigger subject removes the gap and the frame improves, the space was passive: enlarge the subject, or crop it at the edge.

word-colour.instead: say what the colour is for in one clause: "it walks the eye to the product name" passes, "it is on brand" does not. A flash that walks in reading order to the key word is direction; a flash on every word is wallpaper.

world-turns.instead: start a new data-world with a new ground, object and words at least every 2 s; a held 7 s world needs cuts near 2 s (taste/craft/film-structure.md). Change the ground at a cut the film already has; carry the change across the join (a colour that follows the content), never a cold flash. Judge a moving backdrop at 4 or more timestamps, never one still. A ruled grid is a design tool's canvas: use it only if you can say what it does in one clause.

arrival-rhythm.instead: start the next move while the last still settles. Elements in one beat arrive as one phrase, with a tiny anticipation before the main move.

blur-follows-motion.instead: real motion blur makes a word illegible: for type echo the glyph outline in a second colour under the type. A blurred still looks fast; a half-opacity still looks broken.

blur-out-dense.instead: blur out and fade; the blur runs only during the exit itself.

cause-first.instead: move the effect to the frame of its cause (prompts/moves/cursor-click.md: press, then the answer); copy the reference's grammar, not an order that breaks our story. `vawe see` lists the events of a shot next to the nearest sound hit.

constant-camera.instead: hold the camera still and give the hold an element motion: a line typing, a counter, a glint, a secondary action. Keep camera() for the spectacle or a reveal.

entrance-ease.instead: enter(el) from core/motion/presets.js. EASE.land on a handover decelerates through the whole travel and reads as two objects, not one that moved.

entrance-origin.instead: set transform-origin to the point the thing came from. Do not enter everything from one direction with translateY(30px) plus a fade.

exits-shorter.instead: exit on EASE.launch (accelerating) with leave(el) from core/motion/presets.js. An exit on the entrance's own ease arrives while leaving.

follow-through.instead: when the trailing thing is a separate element, delay it as its own move. Stagger is not follow-through: stagger delays siblings.

live-hold.instead: put one element move in every span that sits still over 0.5 s (type a line, tick a counter, pass a glint), never a camera drift (taste/craft/motion-craft.md). Do not fill the hold with a camera drift, push or pan, a scale or translate on a world or stage root, or parallax on the whole ground: the check leaves those out and constant-camera names a camera that never rests. Do not drift data: a chart whose bars drift lies. Judge local motion (something arrives in a small region), not global motion. Do not put the same ambient on every scene, do not loop anything near text being read, and do not pad a scene with ambient motion to look busy: it raises global motion and costs the film. Fix a jolt at the curve that produced it: end the move on a spring or EASE.land, never smooth the number after the fact; a linear camera station or a slow-start curve straight into a hold is the classic shape.

named-eases.instead: swap the keyword or bezier for EASE.land (entrance), EASE.launch (exit) or EASE.carry (move), at most 2 eases per scene (taste/craft/motion-craft.md). The /easing pages may show the nearest bezier as a reference only. Pick the scene ease from the signature (a punchy brand tightens durations and stagger, a calm one stretches them; set it once as :root custom properties).
named-eases.range: EASE.land, landSoft, settle, swap, glide, carry, leave, launch, pop, nudge; sampled springs with 8 or more stops; vary eases like font weights (repeated like elements may take vary), and two layers moving in one beat differ in duration or offset

one-hero-motion.instead: key the hero first at its start and end pose, check the read with nothing else moving, then add secondary and ambient in decreasing loudness. Slide up plus fade is one claim "arriving"; rise plus rotate is two claims about one object: drop one.

overshoot.instead: arrive fast, land soft: EASE.land, or approach(k 0.12 to 0.19). Give about 1 in 3 arrivals a spring: EASE.pop, or curveToLinear(CURVES.overshoot) from core/motion/springs.js. Never on text held for reading (it wobbles). Ease a count with expo-out or quart-out: the deceleration is the weight; counting to a small number is a stunt, cut it.

real-physics.instead: a flap has a hinge, perspective and shading; do not sell a glyph scramble as a flap or one cubic-bezier as an exponential.

spectacle-weak.instead: give the second the Board names the fastest or longest move of the film, with quiet before it. The checks read the Board's Spectacle second, so moving the meta changes nothing.

speed-bands.instead: use bandSeconds(name) and the presets; give the hero gravity or cinematic and the payoff energy. Too many distinct durations read as drift: hold to a few named bands. Give the fastest moves more seconds (the next band) or less distance; keep a quick move for the one element the beat is about.
speed-bands.range: energy 0.15 to 0.3 s; professional 0.3 to 0.5 s; gravity 0.5 to 0.8 s; cinematic 0.8 to 2 s only when the film has the seconds. Reference films peak at 4 to 13 frame heights per second (p10 to p90 of each film's p90). By role: ambient 0.8 to 1.2 s, thesis line 0.5 to 0.8 s, heavy title 0.5 to 0.7 s, caption 0.25 to 0.4 s, payoff snap 0.25 to 0.35 s. Frame counts at 60 fps (finals) or in seconds

stagger.instead: stagger(els) from core/motion/presets.js. Use a seeded shuffle for the order when you want it organic; a gap over 150 ms reads as sluggish. Eight items at 0.10 s run 0.7 s, over the cap.
stagger.range: 30 to 80 ms between siblings (engine default 50 ms); calm 80 to 120 ms. The total (n minus 1) times the gap, so delay = 0.5 / (n minus 1) capped at 80 ms; past about 7 items stagger a few and bring the rest as a block; board cards 60 to 90 ms; a copied product UI follows its measured row gap (`UI.row`, 70 to 100 ms), a film follows this range

camera-path-linear.instead: an eased curve at each stop zeroes velocity and breaks one flight into N hops: compute the tangent at a waypoint key from its neighbours. Each station has a centre, a zoom, a flight time and a dwell.

crossfade-limit.instead: cut, wipe on the motion, or match on a shape. A blend of two still rasters freezes any motion inside its window; use a live join (a shared moving object, a camera travelling through).

cut-on-beat.instead: cut on the action frame (a word lands, a count finishes). Read a user-given track with `vawe sound <track> --cuts <page>`: it gives the beat grid and hits with frame numbers and the second to move each off cut to. If the logo lands at 24:15, pick the tempo that puts a beat there; do not nudge the logo.

eye-trace.instead: in order of cost: place the next headline where the last focal point was; aim the outgoing beat at the corner the next beat opens in; give the next beat more time; keep the jump and say why. Within a beat, move the eye with light (a glow that arrives cold and wide, then tightens and goes hot), with focus (rack from one plane to the other) or with a beam used as a mask; a glow parked on the hero for the whole beat stops being seen within a second.

ground-jump-cover.instead: match the ground to the content; never fade a full-bleed background out (the white flash). Carry the change with a colour that follows the content.

hard-cut-default.instead: be able to say which meaning each accent serves, such as a tone flip or a time jump. Master a few: a dissolve, one momentum move, one zoom, a rare morph. Cut on the beat or two frames early. Use a dissolve for passing time, a fade for an act break, a whip for momentum, a zoom to enter a surface, a match cut for a hidden connection, a morph for a logo or one hero moment.

match-cut-align.instead: cut cleanly, or find the real rhyme.

paired-exit-direction.instead: pair every directional entrance with an exit that continues the same line of travel.

seam-meaning.instead: ask in order: does the seam need to exist; what must the viewer feel; invisible or expressive; what is the relationship (same object new state: morph; rhyme: match cut; time: dissolve; act boundary: fade; opposition: smash cut; new place with energy: whip or wipe). "It looks smoother" is not a reason.

seam-timing.instead: write a ramp with an EASE name (carry into a cut, land out of it). Feather a wipe edge: a hard edge reads as a slide deck. A wipe can sweep at any angle. One velocity personality per film. A handoff eases at both ends: EASE.land on a handover reads as two objects. A blend of the frame before and the frame after turns copy into an unreadable double, so end the outgoing text at the seam. A full-bleed layer above a moving layer must not start mid-move and hide it: start the cover after the move ends, or raise the mover.

seam-variety.instead: change the axis or direction (a wipe on x after a push on y), or cut.
seam-variety.range: moving seams: wipes, pushes, whips, zooms; rotate inside one family (soft, motion, shape, spatial)

gradient-grain.instead: a flat brand gets a flat field. Break the ramp with grain, dither or a dot texture; grain breaks a ramp and film did the same for the same reason. Grain is texture: it is not a ground, not motion and not a fix for a flat frame. Check at the darkest moment and at the brightest glow.

mark-rides-parent.instead: tie the mark to the thing that moves, or delete it the moment it points at nothing.

moving-tail.instead: give one part of the held lockup its own last key (a caret blinks, a value ticks, a highlight moves to the next item), or time one last arrival into the final second. A camera push or a drift on the ground is not a part move (constant-camera). The film has one accent: do not add a second. Do not fade the payoff and do not freeze it.

no-tells.instead: gradient text: one flat colour from the kit. Corner labels and borders: nothing decorates the edge. Glow on UI text: contrast from weight and size. Bursts, rings, split and shake: the subject itself moving. Centred title on a gradient: the title on a real surface, a capture or white space. Template chrome: drop the eyebrow and let the title carry the beat; number only a true sequence; mark a card with space or a surface step, not a stripe; vary the cards in size and weight. A stock device: let the subject carry the beat; a different look, shader or 3D toy every beat is effect soup.

reveal-mask-pad.instead: pad the mask box 0.3 em past the glyph bounds, or reveal with blur and translate and no clip edge.

music-licence.instead: read the contract of a subscription library before buying; add the destination channel to the safelist before posting; use AI-generated music (not copyrightable when purely prompt-made) for internal animatics only. assets/music/ is gitignored; record every track in assets/music/credits.json.

sound-bridge.instead: never butt two sounds; use an equal-power crossfade.

sound-cues.instead: name the visible event behind each cue and cut a cue with none. Time each cue to the page's own beat number (the literal the CSS or seek uses), so a retimed beat moves both. A swell stops dead on the cut it introduces (no tail); a riser ends on the beat and leaves the frame after it quiet. Wall-to-wall hits turn into noise.

sound-level.instead: leave data-gain off. Cue levels are read against each other: a cue that peaks more than 6 dB above or below the median cue draws a warning naming that cue, and the same data-gain shift on every cue moves the loudness without changing the balance, so it is named and is not a fix. A music track the user gave must change over time: one spectrum for the whole film is a drone (the reference films change at least 0.177 on the scale of harness/lib/bed-motion.mjs, a drone 0.002). Measure with `ffmpeg -af ebur128=peak=true`.

sound-voices.instead: take a recorded effect first (the user's file, or the sites in resources/README.md); use a quiet synth tick only when none fits. Before an impact, stop the effects and land the hit into the quiet. To audition the synth voices: `node harness/dev/sound-lab.mjs`.
